headline: High-risk filesystem/MCP pair: Gemini CLI can write and egress broadly, while risingwave is unverified and non-networked, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and compliance uncertainty.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Gemini CLI can use MCP, read/write the filesystem, and process files in cwd; if risingwave outputs are placed in shared files or MCP channels, Gemini could ingest attacker-controlled content as instructions. Risingwave has no documented interactive surface, so the pathway is inferred from Gemini’s documented bridges and the pair’s shared filesystem/git state.
conditions: IF risingwave artifacts are written into a directory Gemini CLI reads
IF an MCP server relays risingwave output into Gemini CLI without provenance tags
mitigations: Disable MCP servers for the session
Keep the two agents on separate directories
Use read-only mounts for any shared artifacts
Require manual review before Gemini consumes risingwave-generated files
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on all shared outputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Gemini CLI touches source code, cwd files, and shell environment, and can egress broadly; risingwave is documented as network-egress none. If both share a workspace, Gemini can read local data and transmit it externally, creating a leakage path even though risingwave itself is not a sender.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the shared cwd
IF Gemini CLI is allowed to send prompts or file contents to external APIs
mitigations: Separate sensitive data from the shared workspace
Run Gemini CLI with network disabled for the task
Restrict file access to a minimal subdirectory
Redact secrets before either agent reads files
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Gemini CLI can write the filesystem and modify git state; the pair shares state via filesystem and git only. Risingwave is unverified and has no documented write surface, so direct conflict is not proven, but the shared mutable repo path makes concurrent edits and git races plausible.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same git checkout
IF risingwave or its orchestration writes to the same files Gemini edits
mitigations: Use separate branches per agent
Serialize edits with a lock file
Commit after each agent finishes
Avoid concurrent runs in the same checkout
requires-engineering: add workspace-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Gemini CLI can generate code or facts from files, and risingwave is a data-engineering system that may consume downstream artifacts. If risingwave treats Gemini output as authoritative, errors can cascade into pipelines or materialized views. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF risingwave ingests Gemini-produced SQL, configs, or summaries without validation
IF Gemini output is used as an upstream source for automated pipeline actions
mitigations: Validate Gemini output before ingestion
Require schema checks on any generated SQL or config
Insert a human approval step before execution
Keep Gemini outputs advisory only
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: Gemini CLI handles source code, files in cwd, and shell environment, while risingwave is an unverified open-source data system with no stated residency or retention controls. No specific regulated-data mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to policy ambiguity rather than a proven breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into the shared workspace
IF organizational policy requires documented retention or residency controls
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Document retention expectations before use
Review logs for sensitive content
Use a non-production dataset
requires-engineering: add explicit residency and retention controls
